topics.note: Whole upper limb: girdle and limb bones (with manubrium, first rib and its cartilage for the sternoclavicular joint and the scalene gap), all joints and ligaments, arm, forearm, hand and shoulder-girdle muscles (pectoralis major/minor, serratus anterior, subclavius, trapezius, latissimus dorsi, levator scapulae, rhomboids) with bursae, tendon sheaths and fasciae incl. pectoral and clavipectoral fascia, scalenus anterior/medius (scalene gap), brachial plexus plus accessory nerve, subclavian/axillary arteries and veins with all limb branches incl. transverse cervical and suprascapular vessels, axillary, cubital, brachial, infraclavicular and interpectoral nodes, and the origin/insertion patches of all these muscles, including the trunk-side origins of the girdle muscles. The superior subscapular nerve is listed by name because the right one is filed under the lumbar plexus in the atlas.

topics.note: Whole lower limb with the bony pelvis (hip bone, sacrum, coccyx): all joints, ligaments and menisci incl. sacro-iliac joint and pubic symphysis, gluteal, hip, thigh, leg and foot muscles with bursae, tendon sheaths, fasciae and retinacula, inguinal ligament, iliopectineal arch and iliopsoas fascia (muscular and vascular lacunae), lumbosacral plexus plus iliohypogastric/ilio-inguinal nerves, external iliac/femoral, gluteal and obturator vessels, inguinal, popliteal and leg nodes, and all lower-limb origin/insertion patches. Excluded: the right superior subscapular nerve (a shoulder nerve misfiled under the lumbar plexus) and the penile dorsal veins inside the great saphenous group.

topics.title: Allgemeine Anatomie
topics.note: General anatomy (terminology, planes, axes, regions, bone types and bone structure) has no structures of its own, so the whole bony skeleton is shown as the reference frame: skull with paranasal sinuses (pneumatised bones), mandible, hyoid, vertebral column, thoracic skeleton with costal cartilages, limb bones with patella and foot sesamoids (sesamoid bones). Teeth, ossicles, laryngeal/nasal cartilages and attachment patches are left out.

topics.title: Gewebe des Bewegungsapparats
topics.note: Tissue histology (bone, cartilage, tendon, skeletal muscle) cannot be shown microscopically, so example organs are shown: long bones, patella, desmally ossifying clavicle and parietal bone, hyaline (costal, thyroid, cricoid, triradiate), elastic (epiglottis) and fibrous cartilage (discs, menisci, labra, interpubic and TMJ discs), tendons/aponeuroses, ligamenta flava and example muscles (biceps brachii, triceps surae).

topics.title: Sehnen und Gelenke
topics.note: General arthrology and tendons: all joints of the skeleton (capsules, ligaments, discs, menisci, labra, syndesmoses, synchondroses, symphyses) with the bones that form them, plus the auxiliary structures and tendon forms: tendon sheaths, bursae, retinacula, aponeuroses (palmar, plantar, epicranial), iliotibial tract, the calcaneal tendon (traction tendon), the extensor digitorum longus tendons and the intermediate tendon of the digastric muscle. Laryngeal joints are left to the larynx topics; sutures are not separate structures.

topics.note: Whole musculoskeletal block (its topic list is not yet published): limbs, spine and trunk wall with all bones, joints and ligaments, limb, girdle, back, thoracic, diaphragm and abdominal-wall muscles with bursae, sheaths, fasciae and attachment patches, scalenes, brachial and lumbosacral plexus, intercostal and lumbar nerves, spinal roots, ganglia, spinal dura and cauda equina, accessory nerve, limb and trunk-wall vessels (subclavian/axillary, femoral, gluteal, obturator, iliolumbar, intercostal, internal thoracic, epigastric, lumbar, azygos) and axillary, inguinal, parasternal, intercostal and inferior epigastric nodes. Head and neck muscles, pelvic floor and genital vessels belong to other blocks and are excluded.

items: Anterior division of internal iliac artery
topics.note: HKL anatomy day = union of the HKL anatomy lectures (mediastinum, heart topography with projection on sternum/ribs, chambers and valves, coronary vessels, cardiac innervation with brainstem and spinal centres, fetal circulation) plus the whole aorta with its first-order branches and the collateral route of aortic coarctation (internal thoracic, superior and inferior epigastric, intercostal arteries). Not in the atlas: pericardium, phrenic nerves, thoracic duct, conduction system, fetal shunts; gonadal arteries left out (male-only parts would force the male body).

topics.note: Anatomy part of the BuA day = the BuA anatomy lecture (lymphatic organs): thymus with its vessels, spleen with splenic vessels and rib projection, palatine tonsils, all lymph node groups, appendix (MALT). Same structures as that lecture on purpose; transfusion medicine, transplantation and inflammation have no atlas structures. Bone marrow, pharyngeal/lingual tonsils and lymph vessels are missing.

Posterior lateral nasal branches of sphenopalatine artery
Posterior septal branches of sphenopalatine artery
topics.note: ATM anatomy day = union of the ATM anatomy lectures: lung with bronchial tree, pulmonary vessels, bronchial-vessel sources and nodes; respiratory apparatus (thoracic skeleton and joints, diaphragm with its openings, respiratory muscles and their attachments, intercostal and phrenic vessels, intercostal nerves, pleura); nose and paranasal sinuses with their relations (upper teeth, hypophysis), vessels, nerves and nodes; larynx (skeleton, joints, membranes, intrinsic muscles and the infrahyoid, suprahyoid, stylopharyngeus and inferior constrictor muscles that move it as a whole) and trachea with neighbours; lung development. Not in the atlas: separate maxillary sinus, vocal folds/conus elasticus, laryngeal and phrenic nerves, superior thyroid artery, bronchial arteries.

topics.title: Herz-Kreislauf-Organe (Einführung, Gefäße, Bildgebende Verfahren)
topics.hint: Kalp için "♥ Kalp çalışma modu": kanın yolu, kapaklar ve oskültasyon noktaları, koroner arterler ve test.
topics.note: IPO circulatory system: whole heart with valves, coronary arteries and cardiac veins, pulmonary circulation, and the main named arteries and veins of the body: aorta with arch branches, coeliac trunk with its three branches, mesenteric and renal arteries, carotid/subclavian/limb arteries with the pulse points, venae cavae, jugular, limb, azygos and portal veins. Vessel histology and imaging have no own structures.

topics.title: Blut und Abwehrsystem 1-3
topics.note: IPO blood and immune system, shown on the lymphoid organs: thymus (primary), spleen with splenic artery and vein, palatine tonsils, all lymph node groups and the appendix as MALT (secondary). Blood cells and bone marrow are not modelled; pharyngeal/lingual tonsils, Peyer patches and lymph vessels are missing.

topics.title: Atmungsorgane 1-3
topics.note: IPO respiratory organs: nasal mucosa, nasal skeleton and paranasal sinuses, pharynx, larynx (cartilages, ligaments/membranes, muscles, epiglottis), trachea, full bronchial tree, lungs, pulmonary vessels, pleura, diaphragm and intercostal muscles. No separate maxillary sinus (part of the maxilla) or vocal folds in the atlas.

topics.title: Mediastinum
topics.note: Mediastinum: contents of all compartments (heart with its coronary arteries and cardiac veins, thymus, great vessels with the aortic-arch branches, thoracic aorta with intercostal arteries, azygos/hemi-azygos system, internal thoracic vessels, trachea and main bronchi, oesophagus, vagus, sympathetic trunk and nerves, mediastinal and parietal thoracic nodes) and its boundaries (sternum, thoracic vertebrae, first ribs of the superior aperture, diaphragm, mediastinal pleura). The heart is shown as in the heart lectures (s3-hkl-3, s3-hkl-5). Not in the atlas: pericardium, phrenic and recurrent laryngeal nerves, thoracic duct, bronchial/oesophageal arteries.

topics.title: Topographie Herz & Perikard
topics.hint: Kalp için "♥ Kalp çalışma modu": kanın yolu, kapaklar ve oskültasyon noktaları, koroner arterler ve test.
topics.note: Heart topography: heart with coronary vessels, the great vessels at its base (arterial and venous pericardial reflections, transverse sinus), sternum, costal cartilages and ribs 1-7 for projecting the heart borders, apex and valve auscultation points onto the intercostal spaces, and the neighbours of the pericardium (diaphragm, oesophagus behind the left atrium, descending aorta, pleura) with the pericardial nodes. Pericardium, pericardial sinuses, phrenic nerves and pericardiacophrenic vessels are not in the atlas.

topics.title: Herzinnenräume
topics.hint: Kalp için "♥ Kalp çalışma modu": kanın yolu, kapaklar ve oskültasyon noktaları, koroner arterler ve test.
topics.note: Heart chambers: both atria and ventricles with papillary muscles, the leaflets of all four valves, and the vessels opening into or leaving the chambers (venae cavae, coronary sinus, four pulmonary veins, pulmonary trunk, ascending aorta). Septa, fossa ovalis, crista terminalis, trabeculae, chordae tendineae and the conduction system are not separate parts.

topics.title: Herzkranzgefäße
topics.hint: Kalp için "♥ Kalp çalışma modu": kanın yolu, kapaklar ve oskültasyon noktaları, koroner arterler ve test.
topics.note: Coronary vessels: left coronary artery with anterior interventricular (septal branches) and circumflex branches, right coronary artery with its inferolateral branch, coronary sinus with great, middle and left-ventricular veins, the aortic root with the coronary leaflets (origin from the aortic sinuses), the pulmonary trunk as landmark of the left main stem, and the atria and ventricles with papillary muscles as supply territories. Small/anterior/smallest cardiac veins and nodal branches are missing.

topics.title: Herzinnervation
topics.hint: Kalp için "♥ Kalp çalışma modu" İleti sekmesinde açılır: ileti sistemi (sinüs düğümü, AV düğümü, His demeti, dallar, Purkinje lifleri) şematik çizilir, uyarı EKG ile eş zamanlı yürür; "Sinirler" kutusu vagus ve sempatik innervasyonu ekler.
topics.note: Cardiac innervation: heart; parasympathetic vagus with its preganglionic nuclei (posterior vagal nucleus, nucleus ambiguus) and the solitary nucleus for visceral afferents (baroreflex); sympathetic preganglionic neurons in the intermediolateral nucleus (T1-T4/5), sympathetic trunk with ganglia and thoracic sympathetic nerves; spinal ganglia for the cardiac pain afferents (referred pain). Cardiac plexus and cervical cardiac nerves are not in the atlas; the conduction system is not a model part but is drawn schematically in the heart study mode (İleti tab).

topics.title: Fetaler Kreislauf
topics.hint: Kalp çalışma modundaki kanın yolu yetişkin dolaşımıdır. Fötal yapılar (foramen ovale, ductus arteriosus, ductus venosus, göbek damarları) modelde yok: ductus arteriosus truncus pulmonalis çatallanmasıyla arkus aortanın arasında, foramen ovale iki kulakçığın arasındadır.
items: Anterior division of internal iliac artery
topics.note: Fetal circulation and its postnatal remnants, shown on the adult vessels: heart (foramen ovale/fossa ovalis region of the atria), venae cavae, liver with portal and hepatic veins (umbilical vein, ductus venosus, ligamentum teres/venosum), pulmonary trunk and arteries (ductus arteriosus to the aortic arch), the preductal arch branches to head and arms, descending aorta and internal iliac arteries with their anterior division (umbilical arteries, medial umbilical ligaments). Placenta, umbilical vessels, ductus venosus/arteriosus and foramen ovale are not modelled.

topics.title: Lymphatische Organe
topics.note: Lymphatic organs (detailed lecture): thymus with its supply (thymic branches of the internal thoracic artery, thymic veins to the left brachiocephalic vein), spleen with splenic artery and vein and its projection onto ribs 9-11, palatine tonsils, all lymph node groups, appendix as gut-associated lymphoid tissue. Bone marrow, pharyngeal/lingual tonsils, Peyer patches (no ileum), splenic ligaments and lymph vessels are not in the atlas.

topics.title: Lunge
topics.note: Lung: lobes, trachea and bronchial tree to the segmental bronchi, pulmonary trunk with pulmonary arteries and veins to the segmental branches (vasa publica), thoracic aorta and azygos vein as source/drain of the bronchial vessels (vasa privata) and, with the aortic arch, as hilum relations, intrapulmonary, tracheobronchial and paratracheal nodes, pleura, vagus and sympathetic trunk (pulmonary plexus). Lung segments as parts, bronchial vessels, bronchopulmonary nodes and the pulmonary plexus are missing.

topics.title: Atemapparat
items: Sternocostal head of pectoralis major muscle (origin)
topics.note: Respiratory apparatus: thoracic skeleton with costovertebral joints and intercostal membranes, diaphragm with its fascia, origins (L1-L3 for the crura) and the structures passing its openings (IVC, oesophagus with vagus, aorta, azygos, sympathetic trunk), intercostal and other thoracic muscles, accessory inspiratory (scalenes, sternocleidomastoid, pectorals, serratus) and expiratory muscles (abdominal wall, quadratus lumborum, latissimus) with their thoracic attachments, intercostal nerves and vessels, internal thoracic and phrenic vessels, azygos system, pleura, parietal thoracic nodes and the superior and inferior diaphragmatic nodes (same diaphragm drainage as the GIT diaphragm dissection s5-git-p10). Phrenic nerve and pleural recesses are not in the atlas.

topics.title: Nase, Nasennebenhöhlen
items: Posterior lateral nasal branches of sphenopalatine artery
Posterior septal branches of sphenopalatine artery
topics.note: Nose and paranasal sinuses: bones of the nasal cavity and sinuses (ethmoid with its cells, frontal and sphenoid with their sinuses, maxilla containing the maxillary sinus, palatine, lacrimal, nasal, inferior concha, vomer), nasal cartilages and mucosa, lacrimal sac and nasolacrimal duct, nasopharynx; relations of the sinuses to the upper premolar/molar roots and to the hypophysis; sphenopalatine, palatine, ethmoidal, labial and facial arteries (Kiesselbach area), facial and ophthalmic veins with the cavernous sinus, olfactory/ophthalmic/maxillary nerves, external nasal muscles, regional nodes. Separate maxillary sinus, conchae as parts and pterygopalatine ganglion are missing.

topics.title: Kehlkopf 1
topics.note: Larynx 1: laryngeal skeleton (thyroid, cricoid, arytenoid and corniculate cartilages, epiglottis, hyoid), joints, ligaments and membranes (thyrohyoid membrane, quadrangular membrane, median cricothyroid ligament), intrinsic laryngeal muscles that move the joints, the extrinsic muscles that raise and lower the larynx as a whole (infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles, stylopharyngeus, and the inferior constrictor arising from the thyroid and cricoid cartilages; the same muscle set as the SOK larynx lecture s6-sok-k), and neighbours (thyroid gland, laryngopharynx). Vocal ligament, conus elasticus and vocal/vestibular folds are not in the atlas.

topics.title: Kehlkopf 2 & Trachea
topics.note: Larynx 2 and trachea: laryngeal muscles on cartilages and ligaments, vagus nerve (recurrent loops around the right subclavian artery and the aortic arch), inferior thyroid artery, superior thyroid vein, deep cervical, pre-/paratracheal and tracheobronchial nodes; trachea with bifurcation and main bronchi and its neighbours (thyroid gland, oesophagus, thymus, aortic arch, brachiocephalic trunk, carotid and subclavian arteries, left brachiocephalic vein, azygos arch). Laryngeal nerves and superior thyroid/laryngeal arteries are not in the atlas.

topics.title: Lungenentwicklung
topics.note: Lung development, shown on the adult derivatives: larynx, trachea and bronchial tree from the respiratory diverticulum, lungs, oesophagus (foregut, tracheo-oesophageal septum and fistulas), pleura (pleural cavities) and diaphragm (pleuroperitoneal membranes, diaphragmatic hernia with lung hypoplasia). Embryonic structures are not modelled.

topics.title: Anatomie (Neuro, drei Lerntage)
groups: Autonomic division of peripheral nervous system
topics.note: ÄBP neuroanatomy (days 20-22) as the union of the 4th-semester neuro lectures and practicals: brain, spinal cord and meninges with all atlas nuclei, tracts and ventricles; cranial nerves I-XII with their branches; spinal roots and ganglia, cauda equina and the segmental nerves used for dermatomes (brachial plexus roots, intercostal, iliohypogastric, ilio-inguinal); sympathetic trunk; hypophysis, pineal gland; arteries of brain and spinal cord from the aortic arch (brachiocephalic trunk, carotids, subclavians, ICA, ophthalmic, ACA/MCA/PCA, vertebrobasilar system, circle of Willis, anterior spinal), middle meningeal artery, dural sinuses with ophthalmic veins, internal jugular vein. Limb plexus branches and eye/ear stay with the BWA and SOK days. Gaps: cerebral veins, insula, internal capsule, substantia nigra, cerebellar and trigeminal nuclei, arachnoid.

topics.title: Schnittbildtrainer
topics.hint: Araçlar › Kesit ile aksiyal, koronal ve sagittal düzlemde kesin; "Dolu" açıkken kesitler BT/MR görüntüsüne benzer. Aksiyal kesitte BT/MR yönü için ⇄ ile üst yarıyı bırakıp kesite alttan (ayak tarafından) bakın; yukarıdan bakış ayna görüntüsüdür.
topics.note: Brain sectional-image trainer (ÄBP day 23): everything that appears in brain sections - cortex, white matter, basal ganglia, diencephalon, ventricles, brainstem with nuclei, cerebellum - plus falx/tentorium, choroid plexus, dural sinuses, hypophysis, pineal gland, optic nerve and the large cerebral arteries (ICA, ACA, MCA, PCA, basilar, vertebral, communicating). The widest of the three imaging topics (s4-neu-p1 has no vessels, s4-neu-2c only landmarks). Gaps: internal capsule, claustrum, insula, substantia nigra, cerebral veins; skull and orbit not included.

topics.title: Neuroanatomie 1-3
groups: Autonomic division of peripheral nervous system
topics.note: IPO nervous-system overview: brain, spinal cord, meninges, cranial nerves I-XII, spinal roots and ganglia, cauda equina, intercostal nerves as the typical segmental spinal nerve, sympathetic trunk, hypophysis, pineal gland, carotid and vertebrobasilar cerebral arteries with circle of Willis, dural sinuses. Limb plexuses are left to the locomotor topics. Gaps: cerebral veins, insula, internal capsule, substantia nigra.

topics.title: Basics Neuroanatomie
topics.note: CNS basics: telencephalon (lobes, gyri, sulci, white matter, basal ganglia, lateral ventricles), diencephalon, brainstem, cerebellum and spinal cord with cauda equina, the 12 cranial nerve trunks at their exits and the spinal roots and ganglia. Nerve branches, meninges and vessels are in their own lectures.

topics.title: Blutversorgung
topics.note: Blood supply of brain and spinal cord: aortic arch, brachiocephalic trunk, carotid and subclavian origins (subclavian steal), internal carotid and ophthalmic arteries, ACA and MCA with cortical and lenticulostriate branches, vertebral/basilar arteries with PICA, AICA, SCA, pontine branches and PCA, communicating arteries, anterior spinal artery; venous drainage through the dural sinuses (cavernous sinus with the ophthalmic veins) to the internal jugular vein. Gaps: anterior choroidal, labyrinthine, posterior spinal and Adamkiewicz arteries, cerebral veins.

topics.title: Architektur Gehirnoberfläche & Subkortex
topics.note: Telencephalon surface and subcortex: all lobar gyri and sulci, interlobar sulci, white matter with corpus callosum, commissures and fornix, caudate, putamen, globus pallidus, amygdala, septal nuclei, lateral ventricles, and the thalamus as the medial border of the internal capsule. Gaps: insular gyri, claustrum, internal/external capsule, association bundles.

topics.title: Bildgebende Topographie
topics.hint: Araçlar › Kesit ile aksiyal, koronal ve sagittal düzlemde kesin; "Dolu" açıkken kesitler BT/MR görüntüsüne benzer. Aksiyal kesitte BT/MR yönü için ⇄ ile üst yarıyı bırakıp kesite alttan (ayak tarafından) bakın; yukarıdan bakış ayna görüntüsüdür.
topics.note: Imaging topography (CT/MRI landmarks, 28 cards): ventricles with septum pellucidum and choroid plexus, caudate, putamen, globus pallidus, thalamus, corpus callosum, fornix, hippocampus, amygdala, central sulcus with pre-/postcentral gyri, lateral sulcus and insular circular sulcus, parieto-occipital and calcarine sulci, midbrain, pons, medulla, cerebellum, optic chiasm, mamillary bodies, hypophysis, pineal gland, falx and tentorium, main dural sinuses and the large cerebral arteries with the circle of Willis. Narrower than the sectional trainer (abp-23): no full gyral map, no brainstem nuclei or tracts. Gaps: internal capsule, insula, claustrum, cerebral veins.

topics.title: Liquor & Meningen
topics.note: CSF and meninges: ventricles, aqueduct, central canal, choroid plexus, septum pellucidum, the circumventricular organs the atlas has (pineal gland, neurohypophysis; blood-CSF barrier part of the lecture), falx cerebri, tentorium, spinal dura, dural sinuses, middle meningeal artery (epidural haematoma), meningeal branch of maxillary nerve, cauda equina (lumbar puncture). Gaps: arachnoid/pia layers, cisterns, arachnoid granulations, interventricular foramen, fourth-ventricle apertures, area postrema.

topics.title: Cerebellum
topics.note: Cerebellum: all lobules, flocculus, tonsils, superior peduncle, fourth ventricle and the tentorium above it, the afferent and efferent relays the atlas has (pons, olive, vestibular nerve and nuclei, spinocerebellar tracts, red nucleus, thalamus) and SCA, AICA, PICA. Gaps: cerebellar nuclei, middle and inferior peduncles, pontine nuclei.

topics.title: Tandem Limbisches System, Lernen
topics.note: Limbic system as a whole (tandem lecture with learning): limbic lobe (cingulate and parahippocampal gyri, hippocampus), amygdala, septal nuclei, fornix, hippocampal commissure, mamillary bodies, thalamus (anterior nuclei), hypothalamus, habenula and stria medullaris, stria terminalis, anterior commissure (Papez circuit, amygdala pathways) and the orbitofrontal cortex (orbital gyri, gyrus rectus). Broader than the hippocampus lecture s4-neu-12. Gaps: dentate gyrus, entorhinal cortex, nucleus accumbens, mammillothalamic tract, cingulum, anterior cingulate gyrus.

topics.title: Hirnstamm & Hirnnerven I
topics.note: Brainstem and cranial nerves I-VI (split assumed from the lecture pair): midbrain, pons, medulla, fourth ventricle, aqueduct, red nucleus, colliculi and the nuclei of III, IV and VI; olfactory, optic (with chiasm and tract), oculomotor, trochlear, trigeminal (roots and three divisions) and abducens nerves. The nuclei of VII-XII belong to s4-neu-8. Gaps: trigeminal nuclei and ganglion, reticular formation, medial lemniscus, MLF.

topics.title: Hirnstamm & Hirnnerven II
topics.note: Brainstem and cranial nerves VII-XII: midbrain, pons, medulla, fourth ventricle and the nuclei of VII-XII (facial, salivatory, vestibular, cochlear, ambiguus, solitary, dorsal vagal, hypoglossal, spinal accessory) plus the abducens nucleus under the facial colliculus (internal facial genu); facial nerve with chorda tympani, vestibulocochlear, glossopharyngeal, vagus, accessory and hypoglossal nerves. The nuclei of III and IV belong to s4-neu-7. Gaps: nervus intermedius, cranial ganglia, named vagal branches, reticular formation.

topics.title: Basalganglien
topics.note: Basal ganglia: caudate, putamen, globus pallidus (lentiform nucleus) and the thalamus as the output station of the loops. Gaps: subthalamic nucleus, substantia nigra, nucleus accumbens, claustrum, internal capsule.

topics.title: Anatomie Rückenmark
topics.note: Spinal cord anatomy: grey matter horns and nuclei, funiculi with all atlas tracts, central canal, anterior and posterior roots, spinal ganglia, cauda equina, spinal dura, anterior spinal artery. Gaps: conus medullaris, filum terminale, arachnoid/pia, denticulate ligaments, posterior spinal and radicular arteries.

topics.title: Funktionelle Systeme Rückenmark
topics.note: Spinal cord pathways: whole cord with ascending and descending tracts and the reflex arc (roots, ganglion, horns), plus the stations along the long pathways: thalamus, pre-/postcentral gyri and paracentral lobule, base of peduncle, pons, medulla with pyramid (corticospinal course and decussations), red nucleus, vestibular nuclei, superior colliculus. Gaps: internal capsule, medial lemniscus, gracile/cuneate nuclei, reticular formation.

topics.title: Zwischenhirn & Basalganglien
topics.note: Diencephalon and basal ganglia: thalamus, geniculate bodies, hypothalamus, mamillary bodies, epithalamus (habenula, stria medullaris, posterior commissure, pineal gland), third ventricle, optic chiasm/tract, hypophysis, fornix (columns dividing the hypothalamus) and stria terminalis (thalamostriate groove), caudate, putamen, globus pallidus. Gaps: thalamic/hypothalamic nuclei, subthalamic nucleus, substantia nigra, internal capsule.

topics.title: Sprache, Sprechen & Lesen
items: Opercular part of inferior frontal gyrus
Triangular part of inferior frontal gyrus
Anterior ascending ramus of lateral sulcus
Anterior horizontal ramus of lateral sulcus
topics.note: Language, speech and reading: Broca area (opercular/triangular inferior frontal gyrus, bounding sulcal rami), Wernicke area (superior temporal gyrus, planum temporale), Heschl gyrus, supramarginal/angular gyri, visual cortex (calcarine sulcus, cuneus, lingual gyrus, occipital pole) and fusiform gyrus, geniculate bodies, corpus callosum, precentral gyrus and articulation nuclei (facial, ambiguus, hypoglossal). Gaps: arcuate fasciculus, insula, SMA.

topics.title: Lernen – Hippocampus & limbisches System
topics.note: Hippocampus and memory: hippocampus in the floor of the inferior horn of the lateral ventricle, parahippocampal gyrus (entorhinal region) with the collateral sulcus, fornix, hippocampal commissure, mamillary bodies, thalamus and cingulate gyrus (Papez circuit), septal nuclei (cholinergic input) and amygdala. The hypothalamic, habenular and orbitofrontal parts of the limbic system are in s4-neu-5. Gaps: dentate gyrus, CA fields, subiculum, entorhinal cortex as its own part, mammillothalamic tract, cingulum.

topics.title: Anatomischer Schmerz
items: Cingulate gyrus and sulcus (Middle anterior part)
topics.note: Pain: posterior root, spinal ganglion, posterior horn, Lissauer tract, anterolateral system (spinothalamic, spinotectal), thalamus, postcentral gyrus, insular region (superior circular sulcus, the only insular part in the atlas), mid-anterior cingulate gyrus, amygdala, trigeminal nerve and sensory root. Gaps: substantia gelatinosa, spinal trigeminal nucleus, periaqueductal grey, raphe nuclei, locus coeruleus, insular gyri.

topics.title: Zusatz: Hirnnervenkerne
topics.note: Cranial nerve nuclei: oculomotor/Edinger-Westphal, trochlear, abducens, facial, salivatory, vestibular, cochlear, ambiguus, dorsal vagal, solitary, hypoglossal and spinal accessory nuclei, with fourth ventricle and aqueduct as landmarks. Gap: trigeminal nuclei.

topics.title: 3D-Neuroanatomie / Radiologie
topics.hint: Araçlar › Kesit ile aksiyal, koronal ve sagittal düzlemde kesin; "Dolu" açıkken kesitler BT/MR görüntüsüne benzer. Aksiyal kesitte BT/MR yönü için ⇄ ile üst yarıyı bırakıp kesite alttan (ayak tarafından) bakın; yukarıdan bakış ayna görüntüsüdür.
topics.note: 3D neuroanatomy/radiology practical: the whole brain for 3D and sectional orientation (lobes, gyri, sulci, white matter, basal ganglia, diencephalon, ventricles, brainstem, cerebellum), choroid plexus, falx/tentorium, hypophysis, pineal gland and optic nerve. Vessels and sinuses are covered by practicals 5 and 6 (s4-neu-p5, s4-neu-p6). Gaps: internal capsule, insula, claustrum.

topics.title: Cerebellum, Hirnstamm, Thalamus
topics.note: Practical: cerebellum (all lobules, superior peduncle), brainstem (midbrain, pons, medulla with nuclei, fourth ventricle, aqueduct), thalamus with geniculate bodies and the third ventricle it borders. Gaps: cerebellar nuclei, middle/inferior peduncles, thalamic nuclei.

topics.title: Hirnnerven 1
topics.note: Cranial nerves practical 1 (I-VI): olfactory, optic with chiasm and tract, oculomotor, trochlear, trigeminal (roots and three divisions) and abducens nerves with their nuclei (oculomotor complex incl. Edinger-Westphal, trochlear, abducens) and exit sites (midbrain with interpeduncular fossa and aqueduct, pons). Gaps: trigeminal ganglion and nuclei, ophthalmic/maxillary branches, ciliary and pterygopalatine ganglia.

topics.title: Hirnnerven 2
topics.note: Cranial nerves practical 2 (VII-XII): facial with chorda tympani, vestibulocochlear, glossopharyngeal, vagus, accessory and hypoglossal nerves with their nuclei (facial, salivatory, vestibular, cochlear, ambiguus, solitary, dorsal vagal, hypoglossal, spinal accessory; abducens nucleus under the facial colliculus) and exit sites (pons, medulla with olive and pyramid, floor of the fourth ventricle). Gaps: nervus intermedius, cranial ganglia, named vagal branches.

topics.title: Topographie Cortex
topics.note: Cortex topography: all gyri and sulci of the frontal, parietal, temporal, occipital and limbic lobes plus interlobar sulci (central, parieto-occipital, lateral-sulcus rami, collateral). Gaps: insular gyri, Brodmann areas.

topics.title: Cerebrale Blutversorgung
topics.note: Cerebral blood supply practical: internal carotid and ophthalmic arteries, ACA and MCA with branches, vertebral/basilar arteries with PICA, AICA, SCA, pontine branches and PCA, communicating arteries, anterior spinal artery, dural sinuses. Gaps: cerebral veins, anterior choroidal and labyrinthine arteries.

topics.title: Meningen und Liquor
topics.note: Meninges and CSF practical: ventricles, aqueduct, central canal, choroid plexus, septum pellucidum, falx cerebri, tentorium, spinal dura, dural sinuses, middle meningeal artery, meningeal branch of maxillary nerve, cauda equina. Gaps: arachnoid/pia layers, cisterns, arachnoid granulations, ventricular foramina.

topics.title: Rückenmark und Dermatome
topics.note: Spinal cord and dermatomes practical: spinal cord (grey matter, tracts, central canal), roots, spinal ganglia, cauda equina, spinal dura and the segmental nerves that map onto dermatomes: brachial plexus roots (C5-T1), intercostal nerves (T1-T11), iliohypogastric and ilio-inguinal nerves (L1). Gaps: dermatome skin maps, conus medullaris, filum terminale, individual spinal nerves and rami.

topics.title: Vegetatives Nervensystem
groups: Autonomic division of peripheral nervous system
topics.note: Autonomic nervous system: sympathetic trunk, ganglia and sympathetic (splanchnic) nerves, adrenal medulla (suprarenal gland, directly innervated by preganglionic fibres), vagus, cranial parasympathetic nerves (III, VII with chorda tympani, IX), autonomic nuclei (Edinger-Westphal, salivatory, dorsal vagal, solitary, intermediolateral, lateral intermediate substance with the sacral parasympathetic nucleus), hypothalamus, abdominal aorta with coeliac and mesenteric trunks marking the prevertebral ganglia. Gaps: prevertebral and parasympathetic ganglia, plexuses, pelvic splanchnic nerves, enteric system.

topics.title: Anatomie Kopf, Mundhöhle, Speicheldrüsen, Pharynx
exclude: Posterior lateral nasal branches of sphenopalatine artery
Posterior septal branches of sphenopalatine artery
topics.note: Head and neck part of the GI tract (GIT lectures 1-3, the head muscle table and the dissections of pharynx/oral cavity, dental apparatus and cervical fasciae): oral cavity with lips and cheeks (orbicularis oris, buccinator), hard palate (maxilla, palatine bone), soft palate, uvula, tongue and tongue muscles, floor of mouth (suprahyoid muscles), teeth, gingiva, palatine tonsil; all major salivary glands with ducts; masticatory apparatus (TMJ with capsule, disc and ligaments, masticatory muscles and their fasciae, mandible, temporal, zygomatic and sphenoid bones) with the origin/insertion areas of the muscle table; pharynx (naso-, oro-, laryngopharynx) with constrictors, stylopharyngeus, palatopharyngeus, auditory tube, epiglottis, hyoid, thyroid and cricoid cartilage, cricopharyngeal ligament and skull-base attachment (occipital bone); cervical fasciae with their contents (investing layer with sternocleidomastoid, trapezius and platysma, infrahyoid muscles, visceral space with thyroid gland, trachea and oesophagus, carotid sheath with common carotid arteries, prevertebral longus and scalene muscles). Nerves: trigeminal trunk, V2, V3 with motor root and branches, VII with chorda tympani, IX, X, XII, and XI with the cervical sympathetic trunk next to ICA and IJV in the parapharyngeal space. Vessels: external carotid with facial, maxillary (without nasal and pterygoid-canal branches), superficial temporal and ascending pharyngeal arteries, inferior thyroid artery; facial, retromandibular, common facial and lingual veins. Nodes: submental, submandibular, parotid, retropharyngeal, upper deep cervical. Missing in atlas: lingual artery, styloglossus, palatoglossus, veli palatini muscles, musculus uvulae, salpingopharyngeus, pharyngeal and lingual tonsil, auriculotemporal nerve, otic and submandibular ganglia, pterygoid venous plexus, pretracheal and prevertebral fascial layers.

topics.title: Anatomie Ösophagus bis Rektum
items: Anterior division of internal iliac artery
topics.note: Oesophagus to anal region (GIT lectures 4-9 with the dissections of the abdominal situs, oesophagus, upper and lower abdominal vessels, stomach/spleen/diaphragm, intestine and rectum): oesophagus with upper sphincter (inferior constrictor, cricoid) and constrictions (aortic arch, left main bronchus, diaphragm), neighbours trachea and left atrium; abdominal situs with omenta, mesocolon and meso-appendix, the intraperitoneal organs incl. liver and gallbladder and the retroperitoneal ones (duodenum with bile and pancreatic ducts, pancreas, kidney, suprarenal gland, ureter, aorta, IVC); stomach with stomach bed (spleen, pancreas, kidney, suprarenal gland); diaphragm with fascia, origins, phrenic, musculophrenic and superior epigastric vessels and diaphragmatic nodes; duodenum, jejunum, colon with taeniae, appendix, sigmoid colon; pelvic floor and external anal sphincter, ischioanal fossa walls (obturator internus, sacrotuberous and sacrospinous ligaments, hip bone, sacrum, coccyx) and the anterior neighbours of the rectum in both sexes (bladder, prostate, seminal glands, ductus deferens / uterus, vagina). Arteries: inferior thyroid, thoracic aorta, coeliac, superior and inferior mesenteric with all branches, inferior phrenic, internal iliac with anterior division and internal pudendal. Veins: portal system, azygos and hemi-azygos (portocaval anastomosis), IVC, internal iliac and internal pudendal. Nodes: deep cervical, paratracheal, tracheobronchial, juxta-oesophageal, all visceral abdominal, diaphragmatic, pararectal, lateral sacral, superficial inguinal. Nerves: vagus, sympathetic trunk, pudendal. Missing in atlas: ileum, caecum, rectum, anal canal, mesentery, internal anal sphincter, puborectalis, oesophageal, right/short gastric, gastro-omental, jejunal, ileal and middle/inferior rectal vessels, thoracic duct.

topics.title: Anatomie Leber, Gallenblase, Pankreas
topics.note: Liver with Couinaud segments, gallbladder, bile duct, pancreas with ducts, duodenum, spleen, lesser omentum, diaphragm (bare area) and the topographic neighbours of liver and pancreas (stomach, kidney, suprarenal gland, transverse colon and mesocolon); coeliac trunk with all branches, superior mesenteric artery with inferior pancreaticoduodenal arteries; portal vein with splenic, superior and inferior mesenteric veins, left renal vein, hepatic veins and IVC; cystic, coeliac, pancreatic, pancreaticoduodenal, splenic and central mesenteric nodes; vagus and sympathetic trunk. Missing in atlas: cystic and hepatic ducts, cystic and right/left hepatic arteries, superior pancreaticoduodenal and pancreatic arteries, liver ligaments, coeliac plexus.

topics.title: Anatomie Niere & ableitende Harnwege bis einschl. Harnblase
topics.note: Kidney and urinary tract up to and including the bladder = union of the urinary lectures, the bladder-closure lecture and the retroperitoneum dissection without the urethra: kidneys, renal pelvis, renal vessels, suprarenal glands, ureters, bladder with trigone; kidney relations (liver, duodenum, pancreas, spleen, colon; diaphragm, psoas, iliacus, quadratus lumborum, transversus, ribs 11-12, lumbar vertebrae, lumbar plexus nerves), ureter crossings, bladder neighbours (prostate, seminal glands, ductus deferens; uterus, vagina); bladder closure (levator ani and coccygeus, pudendal nerve, spinal sympathetic and sacral parasympathetic centres); aorta and IVC with their branches/tributaries, sympathetic trunk, lumbar/iliac/paravesical nodes. Both sexes. Renal fascia, renal plexus, vesical arteries and the urethral sphincters are not in the atlas.

topics.title: Anatomie Weibliche Geschlechtsorgane | Zyklus
items: Anterior division of internal iliac artery
topics.note: Female genital organs and cycle = union of the female HuGO lectures: ovaries, tubes, uterus, vagina, clitoris, vestibular bulbs and glands, female urethra and bladder as neighbours, origin and drainage of the (missing) ovarian vessels (abdominal aorta, IVC, left renal vein, as in s5-hugo-3), internal iliac and pudendal vessels and nerves, inguinal ligament (round ligament), lumbar/iliac/inguinal nodes, pelvic floor, breast with its vessels, nerves and lymph drainage, and hypothalamus with adenohypophysis for the cycle. Female body only. Bony pelvis and ureter left out (their parts have male twins and would block the switch to the female body); ovarian/uterine arteries, broad ligament and labia are missing.

topics.title: Anatomie Männliche Geschlechtsorgane
items: Anterior division of internal iliac artery
topics.note: Male genital organs = union of the male HuGO lectures: testis, epididymis, ductus deferens, seminal glands, ejaculatory ducts, prostate, penis, male urethra, male bladder as neighbour; testicular vessels with their origin/drainage (aorta, IVC, left renal vein: varicocele), internal iliac, internal/external pudendal and penile vessels; pudendal, ilio-inguinal and genitofemoral nerves, inguinal ligament, pelvic floor and external anal sphincter (perineum, as on the female day abp-41); lumbar, iliac and inguinal nodes; hypothalamus and adenohypophysis for the hormonal control. Male body only (female bladder parts excluded; the ureter is left out because its parts have female twins that would block the switch to the male body). Scrotum, spermatic cord coverings, cremaster, bulbo-urethral glands and the other perineal muscles are not in the atlas.

topics.title: Verdauungsapparat 1-3, Bildgebende Verfahren: Verdauung
topics.hint: Araçlar › Kesit ile aksiyal, koronal ve sagittal düzlemde kesin; "Dolu" açıkken kesitler BT/MR görüntüsüne benzer. Aksiyal kesitte BT/MR yönü için ⇄ ile üst yarıyı bırakıp kesite alttan (ayak tarafından) bakın; yukarıdan bakış ayna görüntüsüdür.
topics.note: IPO overview of the digestive system: every digestive organ in the atlas (oral cavity with salivary glands, tongue, palate, teeth, gingiva, tonsil; pharynx; oesophagus; stomach; duodenum, jejunum; colon with taeniae and appendix; liver with segments, gallbladder, bile duct, pancreas with ducts) with tongue, palate and pharyngeal muscles, external anal sphincter, diaphragm (oesophageal hiatus, upper border of the abdominal cavity), omenta, mesocolon and meso-appendix; the unpaired abdominal arteries (coeliac trunk, superior and inferior mesenteric with branches) from the abdominal aorta, portal vein with tributaries, hepatic veins and IVC; vagus and sympathetic trunk. Lymph nodes are left out for the overview. Missing in atlas: ileum, caecum, rectum, anal canal, mesentery.

topics.title: Harnorgane 1-2, Bildgebende Verfahren: Harnorgane
topics.hint: Araçlar › Kesit ile aksiyal, koronal ve sagittal düzlemde kesin; "Dolu" açıkken kesitler BT/MR görüntüsüne benzer. Aksiyal kesitte BT/MR yönü için ⇄ ile üst yarıyı bırakıp kesite alttan (ayak tarafından) bakın; yukarıdan bakış ayna görüntüsüdür.
topics.note: IPO urinary organs: kidneys, renal pelvis, ureters, bladder, male and female urethra, renal vessels, suprarenal glands, aorta and IVC, iliac arteries (ureter constriction where it crosses them), lumbar and paravesical nodes, and the imaging landmarks (lumbar vertebrae, psoas, quadratus lumborum, ribs 11-12). Both sexes; nephron and imaging have no own structures.

topics.title: Geschlechtsorgane 1-2
topics.note: IPO genital organs of both sexes: all male and female genital organs, male urethra, testicular and internal pudendal/penile vessels, pudendal nerve, inguinal and lumbar nodes. Ovarian/uterine vessels, scrotum and labia are not in the atlas.

topics.title: Einführung, Mundhöhle
topics.note: Oral cavity (the general GI introduction has no structures of its own): lips and cheeks (orbicularis oris, buccinator), hard palate (maxilla, palatine bone), soft palate, uvula, palatine tonsil in the isthmus of the fauces, tongue and tongue muscles, floor of mouth (mylohyoid, geniohyoid, digastric, stylohyoid; sublingual and submandibular gland, submandibular duct), opening of the parotid duct, teeth and gingiva, mandible, hyoid. Nerves: lingual nerve, facial nerve with chorda tympani (taste, lip and cheek muscles, posterior digastric), IX and X (tongue root, soft-palate muscles), XII, buccal, inferior alveolar, mental, mylohyoid and maxillary nerves. Vessels: external carotid, facial artery with labial and submental branches, descending/greater palatine, buccal, inferior and posterior superior alveolar and infra-orbital arteries (palate, cheek, teeth); facial, common facial and lingual veins. Nodes: submental, submandibular, jugulodigastric and upper deep cervical. The parotid gland itself belongs to lecture 2. Missing in atlas: lingual artery, styloglossus, palatoglossus, veli palatini muscles, musculus uvulae, lingual tonsil.

topics.title: Speicheldrüsen, Kauapparat
exclude: Posterior lateral nasal branches of sphenopalatine artery
Posterior septal branches of sphenopalatine artery
topics.note: Salivary glands (parotid with accessory gland and duct, submandibular gland and duct, sublingual gland) and masticatory apparatus: TMJ with capsule, disc, lateral, sphenomandibular and stylomandibular ligaments; mandible, temporal, zygomatic and sphenoid bone, maxilla, hyoid; masticatory muscles with masseteric and temporal fascia, suprahyoid muscles (jaw openers); teeth and gingiva. Nerves: trigeminal trunk, motor root and mandibular nerve with all branches in the atlas, maxillary nerve, facial nerve with chorda tympani (course through the parotid, secretion of submandibular and sublingual glands), IX (parotid secretion). Vessels: external carotid, maxillary artery (without nasal and pterygoid-canal branches), superficial temporal with transverse facial artery, facial and submental arteries; retromandibular, facial and common facial veins. Nodes: superficial and deep parotid, submandibular, submental. Missing in atlas: auriculotemporal, masseteric, deep temporal and pterygoid nerves, otic and submandibular ganglia, pterygoid venous plexus, lingual artery.

topics.title: Pharynx
topics.note: Pharynx (naso-, oro-, laryngopharynx) with superior, middle and inferior constrictor, stylopharyngeus and palatopharyngeus, soft palate and uvula, palatine tonsil, auditory tube, tongue root, epiglottis; attachments on hyoid, thyroid and cricoid cartilage (cricopharyngeal ligament) and skull base (occipital, sphenoid, temporal bone). Pharyngeal plexus (IX, X, sympathetic trunk); parapharyngeal (retrostyloid) space with ICA, IJV, IX-XII and the cervical sympathetic trunk. Arteries: external carotid with ascending pharyngeal and facial (ascending palatine) artery, inferior thyroid artery. Nodes: retropharyngeal and upper deep cervical (jugulodigastric). Missing in atlas: pharyngeal and tubal tonsil, salpingopharyngeus, veli palatini muscles, pharyngobasilar and buccopharyngeal fascia, pharyngeal venous plexus, superior thyroid and lingual arteries.

topics.title: Ösophagus
topics.note: Oesophagus (cervical, thoracic, abdominal part) with the upper sphincter (inferior constrictor, Killian triangle) and the three constrictions (cricoid; aortic arch and left main bronchus; diaphragmatic hiatus), neighbours trachea, thoracic aorta, left atrium, and the gastro-oesophageal junction (cardia of the stomach). Arteries: inferior thyroid, thoracic aorta, left gastric, inferior phrenic. Veins: azygos, hemi-azygos, accessory hemi-azygos and portal vein (portocaval anastomosis, oesophageal varices). Nodes: deep cervical, paratracheal, tracheobronchial, juxta-oesophageal, coeliac. Nerves: vagus (oesophageal plexus) and sympathetic trunk. Missing in atlas: oesophageal arteries and veins, left gastric vein, thoracic duct, recurrent laryngeal nerve, vagal trunks as separate parts.

topics.title: Abdominalsitus
topics.note: Abdominal situs: greater and lesser omentum, mesocolon and meso-appendix; intraperitoneal organs (stomach, liver, gallbladder, spleen, jejunum, transverse and sigmoid colon, appendix) and secondarily or primarily retroperitoneal organs (duodenum, pancreas, ascending and descending colon, bile duct, kidneys, suprarenal glands, ureters, aorta, IVC); diaphragm (bare area). Contents of the peritoneal folds and ligaments: hepatoduodenal ligament (proper hepatic artery, portal vein, bile duct), folds of the omental bursa (left gastric and common hepatic artery), splenorenal ligament (splenic artery and vein), transverse mesocolon (middle colic vessels), root of the mesentery (superior mesenteric artery and vein); coeliac trunk and inferior mesenteric artery and vein. Missing in atlas: parietal peritoneum, mesentery, omental bursa, falciform, round and coronary ligaments, ileum, caecum, rectum.

topics.title: Magen
topics.note: Stomach (cardia with the abdominal oesophagus, fundus, body, pylorus to the duodenum) with lesser and greater omentum and the stomach bed (spleen, pancreas, kidney, suprarenal gland, transverse colon and mesocolon, diaphragm); coeliac trunk with left gastric, common and proper hepatic, gastroduodenal and splenic arteries; portal, splenic, left and right gastro-omental and superior mesenteric veins; pyloric, right gastric, right gastro-omental, splenic and coeliac nodes; vagus and sympathetic trunk. Missing in atlas: right gastric, gastro-omental, short gastric and posterior gastric arteries, left and right gastric veins, left gastric and left gastro-omental nodes, vagal trunks, gastrosplenic and gastrocolic ligaments as separate parts.

topics.title: Dünndarm
topics.note: Small intestine: duodenum with its relations (gallbladder at the superior part, right kidney behind and transverse mesocolon in front of the descending part, pancreatic head with bile and pancreatic ducts at the papillae, aorta and IVC behind and superior mesenteric vessels in front of the horizontal part) and jejunum; superior mesenteric, gastroduodenal and inferior pancreaticoduodenal arteries, ileocolic artery with ileal branch; superior mesenteric and portal vein; juxta-intestinal, central superior mesenteric, ileocolic and pancreaticoduodenal nodes; vagus and sympathetic trunk. Missing in atlas: ileum, mesentery, jejunal and ileal arteries and veins, superior pancreaticoduodenal arteries, suspensory muscle of the duodenum.

topics.title: Dickdarm
topics.note: Large intestine: ascending, transverse, descending and sigmoid colon with taeniae, appendix, mesocolon, meso-appendix, greater omentum; superior mesenteric artery with ileocolic (appendicular, colic and ileal branch), right and middle colic and marginal arteries, inferior mesenteric artery with left colic, sigmoid and superior anorectal arteries; superior and inferior mesenteric veins with colic and sigmoid tributaries draining via splenic and portal vein; colic nodes (appendicular, pre- and retrocaecal, ileocolic, paracolic, right, middle and left colic, sigmoid) and central mesenteric nodes, without the small-intestine (juxta-intestinal) nodes; vagus (up to the left colic flexure) and sympathetic trunk. Missing in atlas: caecum, rectum, ileocaecal valve, epiploic appendages, Riolan anastomosis, pelvic splanchnic nerves.

topics.title: Rektum und Analkanal
topics.note: Rectum and anal canal region (both missing in the atlas): sigmoid colon, pelvic diaphragm (levator ani parts, coccygeus), external anal sphincter; superior anorectal artery from the inferior mesenteric artery, internal iliac and internal pudendal vessels, inferior mesenteric vein (portocaval anastomosis); pararectal, lateral sacral, sigmoid and superficial inguinal nodes; pudendal nerve; sacrum, coccyx and the anterior neighbours in both sexes (urinary bladder, seminal glands, ductus deferens, prostate / uterus, vagina). Also missing: internal anal sphincter, puborectalis, anococcygeal ligament, middle and inferior rectal vessels, pelvic splanchnic nerves, inferior hypogastric plexus.

topics.title: Leber & Gallenblase
topics.note: Liver with Couinaud segments, gallbladder, bile duct, lesser omentum (hepatoduodenal ligament), duodenum (papilla), diaphragm (bare area) and the organs that mark the visceral surface (stomach, duodenum, right colic flexure of the transverse colon, kidney, suprarenal gland); aorta and coeliac trunk with common and proper hepatic and gastroduodenal arteries; portal vein with splenic, superior and inferior mesenteric veins; hepatic veins and IVC; cystic and coeliac nodes; vagus and sympathetic trunk (hepatic plexus). Missing in atlas: cystic and hepatic ducts, cystic and right/left hepatic arteries, falciform, round, coronary and triangular ligaments, left gastric and paraumbilical veins, hepatic plexus.

topics.title: Pankreas
topics.note: Pancreas (head, uncinate process, neck, body, tail) with main and accessory pancreatic duct and its topography: duodenal loop with bile duct, stomach in front (omental bursa), root of the transverse mesocolon, spleen at the tail, kidney and suprarenal gland, aorta, IVC and left renal vein behind; coeliac trunk with splenic, common hepatic and gastroduodenal arteries, superior mesenteric artery with inferior pancreaticoduodenal arteries; splenic, superior and inferior mesenteric and portal veins; pancreatic, pancreaticoduodenal, splenic, coeliac and central mesenteric nodes; vagus and sympathetic trunk. Missing in atlas: superior pancreaticoduodenal and pancreatic (dorsal, great, caudal) arteries, coeliac and mesenteric ganglia and plexus.

topics.title: Muskeltabelle
topics.note: GIT muscle table (head): masticatory, suprahyoid, tongue, soft-palate and pharyngeal muscles plus buccinator and orbicularis oris, with the origin and insertion areas the atlas has (masseter, temporalis, medial pterygoid, mylohyoid, geniohyoid, anterior digastric, buccinator, orbicularis oris), the bones of attachment and the motor nerves: V3 (motor root, anterior division, nerve to mylohyoid), VII (posterior digastric, stylohyoid, buccinator), IX (stylopharyngeus), X (constrictors and palatopharyngeus via the pharyngeal plexus), XII (tongue muscles). Missing in atlas: styloglossus, palatoglossus, tensor and levator veli palatini, musculus uvulae, salpingopharyngeus, attachment areas of lateral pterygoid, posterior digastric and stylohyoid.

topics.title: Abdominalsitus
topics.note: Abdominal situs dissection: greater and lesser omentum, mesocolon, meso-appendix; stomach, liver, gallbladder, spleen, pancreas (seen through the opened omental bursa), duodenum, jejunum, colon with taeniae and appendix, diaphragm; hepatoduodenal ligament (proper hepatic artery, portal vein, bile duct) with the IVC behind the omental foramen, folds of the omental bursa (left gastric and common hepatic artery), splenorenal ligament (splenic artery and vein), root of the mesentery (superior mesenteric artery and vein). Retroperitoneal organs behind the parietal peritoneum are left to the retroperitoneum dissection. Missing in atlas: mesentery, ileum, caecum, omental bursa, parietal peritoneum, falciform and round ligaments.

topics.title: Pharynx und Mundhöhle
topics.note: Pharynx and oral cavity dissection: pharynx opened from behind with constrictors, stylopharyngeus, palatopharyngeus and its skull-base attachment (occipital, sphenoid, temporal bone), soft palate, uvula, palatine tonsil, auditory tube, epiglottis, hyoid and laryngeal cartilages; parapharyngeal space with ICA, IJV, IX, X, XI, XII and cervical sympathetic trunk; oral cavity with lips and cheeks, hard palate, tongue and its muscles, floor of mouth (suprahyoid muscles, sublingual and submandibular gland, submandibular duct, lingual nerve, chorda tympani, XII, lingual vein), opening of the parotid duct, gingiva. Arteries: external carotid, ascending pharyngeal, facial, inferior thyroid. Nodes: submental, submandibular, retropharyngeal, upper deep cervical. The parotid gland itself is not part of this dissection. Missing in atlas: lingual artery, pharyngeal tonsil, styloglossus, veli palatini muscles, superior cervical ganglion as a separate part.

topics.title: Ösophagus
topics.note: Oesophagus dissection in the neck, the posterior mediastinum and at the hiatus: oesophagus with inferior constrictor and cricoid, trachea, left main bronchus, aortic arch, thoracic aorta, left atrium, diaphragm and cardia of the stomach; inferior thyroid, left gastric and inferior phrenic arteries; azygos, hemi-azygos and accessory hemi-azygos veins; vagus (oesophageal plexus) and thoracic sympathetic trunk; paratracheal, tracheobronchial and juxta-oesophageal nodes. Missing in atlas: oesophageal branches, thoracic duct, recurrent laryngeal nerve, splanchnic nerves.

topics.title: Gefäßversorgung Unterbauch
topics.note: Lower abdominal blood supply: superior mesenteric artery with inferior pancreaticoduodenal, ileocolic (appendicular, colic, ileal branch), right and middle colic and marginal arteries; inferior mesenteric artery with left colic, sigmoid and superior anorectal arteries; superior and inferior mesenteric veins with colic and sigmoid veins draining via splenic and portal vein; aorta, IVC, mesenteric nodes and the supplied intestines (duodenum, jejunum, colon, appendix). Missing in atlas: jejunal and ileal vessels, Riolan anastomosis, ileum, caecum, mesentery.

topics.title: Zahnapparat
topics.note: Dental apparatus: permanent teeth (incisors, canines, premolars, first and second molars), gingiva, alveolar processes of maxilla and mandible; inferior alveolar nerve with mental nerve and nerve to mylohyoid, maxillary nerve (superior alveolar supply); inferior alveolar (mental and mylohyoid branches), posterior superior alveolar and infra-orbital arteries; submandibular nodes. Missing in atlas: third molars, deciduous teeth, periodontium, superior alveolar nerves.

topics.title: Gefäßversorgung Oberbauch
topics.note: Upper abdominal blood supply: coeliac trunk with left gastric, common and proper hepatic, gastroduodenal and splenic arteries, inferior phrenic artery, superior mesenteric artery with inferior pancreaticoduodenal arteries (pancreaticoduodenal arcade); portal vein with splenic, gastro-omental and superior mesenteric veins; the supplied organs (stomach, liver, gallbladder, bile duct, spleen, pancreas, duodenum, lesser omentum) and upper abdominal nodes. Missing in atlas: right gastric, gastro-omental, short gastric, cystic and superior pancreaticoduodenal arteries, left and right gastric veins.

topics.title: Halsfaszien
topics.note: Cervical fasciae: superficial investing layer (the only cervical fascia in the atlas) with sternocleidomastoid, trapezius and the subcutaneous platysma; pretracheal layer with the infrahyoid muscles; visceral space (thyroid gland, larynx with thyroid and cricoid cartilage, trachea, laryngopharynx, oesophagus); carotid sheath (common carotid arteries, IJV, vagus); prevertebral layer with longus and scalene muscles and the cervical sympathetic trunk with its ganglia; nodes of the retropharyngeal space. Missing in atlas: pretracheal and prevertebral layers, carotid sheath, buccopharyngeal fascia, ansa cervicalis, phrenic nerve.

topics.title: Leber & Gallenblase
topics.note: Liver and gallbladder dissection: liver with segments and the neighbours that mark it (stomach, duodenum, transverse colon, kidney, suprarenal gland), gallbladder, bile duct, lesser omentum with the hepatoduodenal ligament (proper hepatic artery, portal vein, bile duct, hepatic branches of the vagus), diaphragm; coeliac trunk with common and proper hepatic and gastroduodenal arteries; portal vein with its main tributaries, hepatic veins, IVC; cystic and coeliac nodes. The sympathetic trunk is not part of this dissection. Missing in atlas: cystic and hepatic ducts, cystic and right/left hepatic arteries, borders of the Calot triangle, liver ligaments.

topics.title: Magen, Milz & Zwerchfell
topics.note: Stomach, spleen and diaphragm dissection: stomach with omenta, abdominal oesophagus and duodenum, stomach bed and splenic neighbours (pancreas, kidney, suprarenal gland, transverse colon and mesocolon); diaphragm with fascia, origin areas, phrenic and musculophrenic vessels and diaphragmatic nodes; structures passing it (oesophagus with vagus, aorta, IVC, azygos and hemi-azygos veins, sympathetic trunk, superior epigastric vessels in the sternocostal triangle); coeliac trunk with all branches in the atlas, portal, splenic, gastro-omental and superior mesenteric veins; pyloric, gastric, gastro-omental, splenic and coeliac nodes. Missing in atlas: phrenic and splanchnic nerves, thoracic duct, short gastric and gastro-omental arteries, gastrosplenic and splenorenal ligaments.

topics.title: Darm
topics.note: Intestine dissection: duodenum with pancreas, bile duct and pancreatic ducts (papillae), jejunum, colon with taeniae and appendix, mesocolon, meso-appendix, greater omentum; superior and inferior mesenteric arteries with all branches in the atlas, gastroduodenal artery, superior and inferior mesenteric veins with tributaries, portal vein, aorta; mesenteric and pancreaticoduodenal nodes. Autonomic nerves are not part of this dissection (the atlas has no mesenteric plexus). Missing in atlas: ileum, caecum, mesentery, jejunal and ileal vessels.

topics.title: Pankreas
topics.note: Pancreas dissection: pancreas with its ducts exposed through the omental bursa, duodenum, bile duct, stomach, transverse mesocolon, spleen, kidney and suprarenal gland; coeliac trunk with splenic, common hepatic and gastroduodenal arteries, superior mesenteric and inferior pancreaticoduodenal arteries; splenic, superior and inferior mesenteric, portal and left renal veins, aorta and IVC; pancreatic, pancreaticoduodenal, splenic, coeliac and central mesenteric nodes. Autonomic nerves are not part of this dissection. Missing in atlas: superior pancreaticoduodenal and pancreatic arteries, coeliac and mesenteric ganglia.

topics.title: Rektum
items: Anterior division of internal iliac artery
topics.note: Rectum dissection (rectum and anal canal missing in the atlas): sigmoid colon, pelvic diaphragm, external anal sphincter, walls of the ischioanal fossa (obturator internus with the pudendal canal, sacrotuberous and sacrospinous ligaments, hip bone, sacrum, coccyx); superior anorectal artery, inferior mesenteric, internal iliac (anterior division) and internal pudendal vessels, inferior mesenteric vein; pararectal, lateral sacral, sigmoid and superficial inguinal nodes; pudendal nerve; male and female pelvic neighbours. Also missing: internal sphincter, puborectalis, middle and inferior rectal vessels, pelvic autonomic nerves.

topics.title: Topographie, Histologie Niere und ableitende Harnwege
topics.note: Kidney and urinary tract (topography; histology has no own parts): kidneys, renal pelvis, renal vessels, suprarenal glands with their arterial sources (inferior phrenic, aorta, renal arteries), ureters, bladder, male urethra with prostate, corpus spongiosum and glans, female urethra; kidney relations in front (liver, duodenum, pancreas, spleen, colic flexures on ascending/descending colon) and behind (diaphragm, psoas, quadratus lumborum, transversus, ribs 11-12, iliohypogastric/ilio-inguinal/genitofemoral nerves); ureter crossings (gonadal and iliac vessels, ductus deferens); bladder neighbours (prostate, seminal glands; uterus, vagina); great vessels, sympathetic trunk, lumbar/iliac/paravesical nodes. Both sexes. Renal fascia/fat capsule, ovarian and uterine vessels are missing.

topics.title: Histologie und Funktion von Hoden etc.
topics.note: Histology and function of the testis and male tract, shown on the organs: testis, epididymis, ductus deferens, seminal glands, ejaculatory ducts, prostate, penis with the male urethra, testicular arteries and veins (pampiniform plexus), and hypothalamus and adenohypophysis for the hormonal control (GnRH, LH/FSH). Male body only; microscopic structures are not modelled.

topics.title: Weibliche und männliche Geschlechtsorgane
items: Anterior division of internal iliac artery
topics.note: Female and male genital organs (macroscopic): all genital organs of both sexes, male urethra, female urethra with its orifice; gonadal vessels with their origin/drainage (aorta, IVC, left renal vein), internal iliac vessels with their anterior division (origin of the uterine, vaginal, vesical and internal pudendal arteries), internal/external pudendal and penile vessels; pudendal, ilio-inguinal and genitofemoral nerves, inguinal ligament (inguinal canal), pelvic floor and external anal sphincter (perineum, as in the female and male ÄBP days); ureter and bladder as neighbours (ureter crossings, vesico-uterine relations); lumbar, iliac and inguinal nodes. Both sexes. Ovarian/uterine arteries, broad ligament, scrotum, labia and the other perineal muscles are missing.

topics.title: Entwicklung der Harn- und männlichen Geschlechtsorgane
topics.note: Development of the urinary and male genital organs, shown on the adult derivatives: kidneys, renal pelvis, ureters, bladder, urethra (both sexes), testis, epididymis, ductus deferens, seminal glands, ejaculatory ducts, prostate, penis; testicular vessels and inguinal ligament (descent of the testis); aorta with renal, common iliac and inferior mesenteric arteries (ascent of the kidney, accessory renal arteries, horseshoe kidney held by the IMA). The male organs show on the male body; embryonic structures are not modelled.

topics.title: Histologie Ovar, Eileiter, Uterus und hormonelle Steuerung
topics.note: Histology of ovary, uterine tube and uterus and their hormonal control, shown on the organs: ovaries, tube parts, uterus parts, plus hypothalamus and adenohypophysis for the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis. Female body only; endometrium, follicles and corpus luteum are not modelled.

topics.title: Retroperitonealraum und Nieren
topics.note: Dissection of the retroperitoneum and kidneys: kidneys, renal pelvis, ureters, suprarenal glands, abdominal aorta with parietal and visceral branches, renal and gonadal vessels, IVC with lumbar and ascending lumbar veins, lumbar, common iliac and inferior diaphragmatic nodes, sympathetic trunk, lumbar plexus nerves, posterior abdominal wall (psoas, iliacus, quadratus lumborum, transversus, diaphragm, iliopsoas fascia, 12th rib). Both sexes. Cisterna chyli, subcostal nerve, renal fascia and ovarian vessels are missing.

topics.title: Mamma
topics.note: Breast: mammary gland lobes, lactiferous ducts and sinuses, nipple, areola, fat and suspensory ligaments; supply by internal thoracic, lateral thoracic, thoraco-acromial (pectoral branches) and intercostal vessels from the axillary vessels; intercostal nerves; lymph drainage to axillary, interpectoral, infraclavicular, supraclavicular and parasternal nodes; bed and axillary dissection (pectoral fascia, pectoralis major/minor, serratus anterior, long thoracic nerve, thoracodorsal nerve and vessels). Female body only.

topics.title: Vulva, Vagina und Cervix
items: Anterior division of internal iliac artery
topics.note: Vulva, vagina and cervix: clitoris, vestibular bulbs, greater vestibular glands, female urethra with its orifice, vagina with fornix, cervix with both ora, female bladder as anterior neighbour; internal iliac vessels with their anterior division (origin of the vaginal and uterine arteries), internal/external pudendal vessels, pudendal, ilio-inguinal and genitofemoral (genital branch) nerves; inguinal (vulva) and iliac (vagina, cervix) nodes; levator ani and external anal sphincter. Female body only. Labia, hymen, vaginal/uterine arteries and the other perineal muscles are missing.

topics.title: Schwangerschaft
topics.note: Pregnancy: uterus, uterine tubes, ovaries, vagina, vulva (vestibular bulbs and glands) and the pelvic floor with external anal sphincter (soft birth canal). Female body only. Placenta, fetal membranes and umbilical cord are not modelled; the bony pelvis is left out because its parts have male twins that would block the switch to the female body.

topics.title: Blasenverschluss
topics.note: Bladder closure (continence): bladder of both sexes with trigone and ureteric orifices, male and female urethra, prostate, levator ani and coccygeus (pelvic floor), pudendal nerve (external sphincter), sympathetic trunk, the intermediolateral nucleus (sympathetic T10-L2) and the lateral intermediate substance (sacral parasympathetic nucleus S2-S4 for the detrusor; same spinal centres as the autonomic lecture s5-git-vns). Internal/external urethral sphincters, detrusor, pelvic splanchnic and hypogastric nerves and the micturition centres are not in the atlas.

topics.title: Anatomie | Biochemie (Endokrinium)
topics.note: Union of the semester-6 endocrine anatomy lectures 1-5: hypothalamus and hypophysis with the sella region (sphenoid sinus, optic chiasm, cavernous/intercavernous sinuses, internal carotid artery, cerebral arterial circle, nerves III-VI), pineal gland with epithalamus and aqueduct, target organs of the pituitary axes (thyroid, adrenals, gonads, liver, mammary gland), thyroid and parathyroids with vessels, nodes, infrahyoid muscles and laryngotracheal neighbours, adrenal glands with kidney and vessels, endocrine pancreas with duodenum, spleen, coeliac/mesenteric/portal vessels and pancreatic nodes, and the host organs of the diffuse endocrine system (lecture 4: stomach, small intestine, colon, cardiac atria, kidney, liver, thymus). Superior thyroid/suprarenal arteries and adrenal veins are not in the atlas; biochemistry has no structures.

topics.title: Anatomie (SOK)
topics.note: Union of the semester-6 SOK lectures and practicals: skull osteology (cranium, mandible, hyoid); orbit and eye (bulb, lacrimal apparatus, eyelids, extra-ocular muscles, nerves II-VI, ophthalmic vessels, angular vessels) with visual pathway and reflex nuclei; ear (tympanic membrane, ossicles, tube, cochlea, vestibule, nerves VII/VIII, temporal bone and neighbouring vessels, auricular nodes) with auditory and vestibular pathways; taste and smell with gustatory (subcentral, insular) and olfactory cortex; larynx with cartilages, membranes, intrinsic, infra- and suprahyoid muscles, vagus, deep anterior and deep lateral cervical nodes and neighbours. Microscopic receptor structures are not in the atlas.

topics.title: Endokrines System 1-2
topics.note: Overview of the endocrine organs: hypothalamus, adeno- and neurohypophysis, pineal gland, thyroid, parathyroids, adrenal glands, pancreas and gonads. Follicles, islets and cortical zones are microscopic.

topics.title: Sinnesorgane 1-2
topics.note: Overview of the sense organs with their main pathways: eye (bulb, lacrimal apparatus, extra-ocular muscles) with the visual pathway to the calcarine cortex; ear (tympanic membrane, ossicles, auditory tube, cochlea, vestibule, nerve VIII) with cochlear and vestibular nuclei, inferior colliculus, medial geniculate body and Heschl gyrus; smell (olfactory nerve, nasal mucosa); taste (tongue, facial nerve with chorda tympani, glossopharyngeal nerve, solitary nucleus). Receptor cells are microscopic.

topics.title: Epiphyse, Hypophyse
topics.note: Pineal gland with epithalamus (habenula, stria medullaris, posterior commissure), third ventricle, superior colliculi and the aqueduct (compressed by pineal tumours); adeno- and neurohypophysis with hypothalamus and mamillary bodies, optic chiasm and tract, sella and sphenoid sinus, cavernous and intercavernous sinuses with internal carotid artery and nerves III, IV, V1, V2, VI, and the cerebral arterial circle around the infundibulum. Pituitary stalk, portal vessels, hypophyseal arteries and hypothalamic nuclei are not in the atlas.

topics.title: Hormonelle Achsen
topics.note: Hypothalamic-pituitary axes: hypothalamus, adeno- and neurohypophysis and the target organs of the thyrotropic, corticotropic, gonadotropic, somatotropic and lactotropic axes: thyroid, adrenal glands, testes and ovaries, liver (IGF-1 source) and mammary gland. Mostly physiology; hormones and feedback loops have no structures.

topics.title: Periphere endokrine Organe
topics.note: Peripheral endocrine glands: adrenal glands with kidney and vessels (inferior suprarenal and inferior phrenic arteries, aorta, left renal vein, IVC); endocrine pancreas with its ducts, duodenum and spleen as neighbours, coeliac trunk with common hepatic, gastroduodenal and splenic arteries, superior mesenteric and inferior pancreaticoduodenal arteries, splenic, superior mesenteric and portal veins (islet hormones reach the liver first), pancreatic and pancreaticoduodenal nodes; parathyroid glands on the thyroid gland; gonads. Superior/middle suprarenal arteries, superior pancreaticoduodenal arteries and adrenal veins are missing; islets and cortical zones are microscopic.

topics.title: Peripheres endokrines System
topics.note: Read as the diffuse (disseminated) endocrine system; the cells are microscopic, so the host organs are shown: stomach, duodenum, jejunum and colon with appendix (enteroendocrine cells), pancreas, cardiac atria (ANP), kidney (renin, erythropoietin), liver (IGF-1, angiotensinogen; whole organ without the Couinaud segments) and thymus. Interpretation of the title is uncertain; the ileum is not in the atlas.

topics.title: Schilddrüse
topics.note: Thyroid gland with parathyroids, inferior thyroid artery and thyrocervical trunk, external carotid artery (origin of the missing superior thyroid artery), superior thyroid vein to the internal jugular vein and the left brachiocephalic vein (drainage of the missing inferior thyroid veins), carotid sheath (common carotids, internal jugular vein, vagus), thyroid/pre-/paratracheal nodes, infrahyoid muscles, and neighbours (thyroid/cricoid cartilages, median cricothyroid ligament, hyoid, trachea, oesophagus). Superior thyroid artery, middle/inferior thyroid veins and the laryngeal nerves are not in the atlas.

topics.title: Einführung in den SB
topics.note: Block introduction (no cards yet): overview of its organs: eye with extra-ocular muscles and lacrimal apparatus, ear with ossicles and nerve VIII, olfactory nerve and nasal mucosa, tongue, larynx cartilages and epiglottis.

topics.title: Histologie Auge
topics.note: Eye histology: the eyeball parts in the atlas (cornea, sclera, iris, lens, zonular fibres, chambers, vitreous, retina) with optic nerve, central retinal and posterior ciliary arteries, the eyelid layers (tarsi, palpebral orbicularis oculi, levator palpebrae) and the lacrimal apparatus. Choroid, ciliary body, conjunctiva and retinal layers are not separate structures.

topics.title: Histologie Cochlea
topics.note: Cochlea histology: only the cochlea as a whole with the cochlear and vestibulocochlear nerves (both sides) exists in the atlas; organ of Corti, scalae, stria vascularis and spiral ganglion are microscopic.

topics.title: Ohr 1
topics.note: Outer and middle ear: tympanic membrane, ossicles, auditory tube with nasopharynx, temporal bone, facial nerve and chorda tympani, tympanic-cavity neighbours (internal carotid, internal jugular vein, sigmoid sinus), auricular vessels and pre-/infra-auricular and mastoid nodes. Auricle, meatus, tympanic cavity and middle-ear muscles are not in the atlas.

topics.title: Geschmackssinn und Geruchssinn
topics.note: Taste: tongue, soft palate, epiglottis, chorda tympani/lingual, facial, glossopharyngeal and vagus nerves, solitary nucleus, thalamus and gustatory cortex (subcentral gyrus, insula via its circular sulcus). Smell: nasal mucosa, ethmoid bone, olfactory nerve/bulb in the olfactory sulcus, gyrus rectus, orbitofrontal gyri, amygdala, parahippocampal (entorhinal) gyrus, anterior commissure, ethmoidal arteries. Taste buds and olfactory epithelium are microscopic; insular gyri are not modelled separately.

topics.title: Ohr 2
topics.note: Inner ear: cochlea and vestibule in the temporal bone, ossicles (stapes at the oval window), vestibulocochlear nerve with cochlear and vestibular parts, facial nerve with chorda tympani (internal acoustic meatus), anterior inferior cerebellar artery (origin of the labyrinthine artery). Semicircular canals, membranous labyrinth and labyrinthine artery are not in the atlas.

topics.title: Hörbahn und Vestibularorgan
topics.note: Auditory pathway: cochlea, cochlear nerve, cochlear nuclei, inferior colliculus, medial geniculate body, Heschl gyrus, planum temporale, superior temporal gyrus. Vestibular system: vestibule, vestibular nerve and nuclei, vestibulospinal tracts, flocculus and nodulus, eye-muscle nuclei of the vestibulo-ocular reflex. Superior olive, lateral lemniscus, MLF and semicircular canals are missing.

topics.title: Orbita
topics.note: Orbit: orbital bones (frontal, ethmoid with cells, sphenoid, zygomatic, maxilla, lacrimal, palatine) with frontal/sphenoid sinuses, eyeball, lacrimal apparatus, extra-ocular muscles with levator, common tendinous ring, trochlea and tarsi, orbicularis oculi, nerves II, III, IV, VI, ophthalmic and maxillary nerves, ophthalmic artery with all branches, infra-orbital artery, angular artery and vein (facial anastomoses), ophthalmic veins and cavernous sinus with the internal carotid artery. Ciliary ganglion and V1 branches are not in the atlas.

topics.title: Auge und Sehbahn
topics.note: Eye and visual pathway: eyeball, optic nerve, chiasm and tract, lateral geniculate body, visual cortex around the calcarine sulcus (cuneus, lingual gyrus, occipital pole) with the posterior cerebral artery, central retinal artery, and the pupillary reflex path (superior colliculus, Edinger-Westphal and oculomotor nuclei, oculomotor nerve). Optic radiation and pretectum are missing.

topics.title: Osteologie (Schädel)
topics.hint: Kafatası kemiklerini tek tek seçip "Karşı tarafı da seç" ile iki yanı birlikte görün; Saydam katmanla iç kafa tabanı da görünür.
topics.note: Skull osteology: all neuro- and viscerocranial bones with paranasal sinuses and ethmoidal cells, mandible and hyoid. Foramina, fossae and sutures are features on these bones; teeth belong to the dental topics.

topics.title: Ohr
topics.note: Ear practical: temporal bone with tympanic membrane, ossicles, auditory tube and nasopharynx, cochlea and vestibule, vestibulocochlear and facial nerves with chorda tympani, and the vessels bordering the tympanic cavity (internal carotid, internal jugular vein, sigmoid sinus).

topics.title: Auge 1
topics.note: First eye practical (orbit dissection): deliberately the same scope as the Orbita lecture, since the practical demonstrates exactly that region: orbital bones, eyeball, lacrimal apparatus, extra-ocular muscles and levator, eyelid muscle, nerves II-VI with V1/V2, ophthalmic artery and branches, angular artery and vein, ophthalmic veins, cavernous sinus with internal carotid artery. The eyeball/eyelid detail and the visual pathway are the second practical. Ciliary ganglion and frontal/lacrimal/nasociliary nerves are missing.

topics.title: Auge 2
topics.note: Second eye practical (no cards yet; scope inferred): eyeball, eyelids (tarsi, levator, orbicularis oculi), lacrimal apparatus, retinal/ciliary arteries and the visual pathway (optic nerve, chiasm, tract, lateral geniculate body, visual cortex).

topics.title: Kehlkopf Anatomie
topics.note: Larynx: thyroid, cricoid, arytenoid and corniculate cartilages, epiglottis, hyoid; thyrohyoid and quadrangular membranes, median cricothyroid ligament; all intrinsic laryngeal muscles, the muscles moving the larynx as a whole (infrahyoid and suprahyoid muscles, stylopharyngeus) and the inferior constrictor; vagus nerve, inferior thyroid artery, superior thyroid vein; lymph drainage to the deep anterior cervical (pre-/paratracheal, thyroid) and the upper and lower deep lateral cervical nodes (supra- and subglottic drainage, as in the ATM larynx lectures); laryngopharynx, trachea and thyroid as neighbours. Vocal folds, laryngeal nerves and mucosa are not in the atlas.
